**Proof.**

Yes, such a one-form exists. We construct it using a partition of unity.

**Local construction.** Since $Z$ is nowhere zero, for every $p \in M$ there is an open neighborhood $U_p$ on which $Z$ remains nowhere zero (by continuity of $Z$). On such a $U_p$, we can complete $Z$ to a local frame: choose vector fields $X_2, \dots, X_n$ on a possibly smaller neighborhood $U_p' \subseteq U_p$ so that $\{Z, X_2, \dots, X_n\}$ is a frame for $TM$ over $U_p'$. (This is possible: pick any frame at $p$ where $Z(p)$ is the first element, then extend by a standard argument using local triviality of the tangent bundle and the fact that $Z \neq 0$ gives a nonvanishing section to start from.)

Define the local one-form $\gamma_p \in \Omega^1(U_p')$ to be the dual of $Z$ in this frame:
$$\gamma_p(Z) = 1, \qquad \gamma_p(X_i) = 0 \;\;(i = 2, \dots, n).$$
This is smooth since it is defined by a smooth frame.

**Global construction via partition of unity.** The collection $\{U_p'\}_{p \in M}$ is an open cover of $M$. Since $M$ is a smooth manifold (hence paracompact), there is a locally finite refinement $\{U_\alpha\}$ and a smooth partition of unity $\{\rho_\alpha\}$ subordinate to it, with $\sum_\alpha \rho_\alpha = 1$ and $\operatorname{supp}(\rho_\alpha) \subseteq U_\alpha$.

On each $U_\alpha$ we have the local one-form $\gamma_\alpha$ with $\gamma_\alpha(Z) = 1$. Define the global one-form
$$\gamma = \sum_\alpha \rho_\alpha \, \gamma_\alpha.$$
This sum is locally finite, so $\gamma$ is a well-defined smooth one-form on all of $M$. Evaluating on $Z$:
$$\gamma(Z) = \sum_\alpha \rho_\alpha \, \gamma_\alpha(Z) = \sum_\alpha \rho_\alpha \cdot 1 = \sum_\alpha \rho_\alpha = 1.$$

Thus $\gamma(Z) = 1$ everywhere on $M$. $\blacksquare$

### PROOF COMPLETE
